Origin and structure

r: **Young fold mountains** of tectonic origin – the **geologically young and unstable** landmass of India
Raised from **Tethys (geosynclinal)** sediments in the **Tertiary** (Eocene–Pliocene) as the **Indian plate** pushed into Eurasia (~70 million years ago, still rising)
**Himadri folds are asymmetrical** with a **granite** core; **steep slope faces the plains**, gentle slope faces Tibet
The Indus and Sutlej are older than the Himalaya and cut gorges through it
Greater Himalaya sedimentary rocks fossil-less; marine fossils in the Lesser Himalaya; remains of human civilisation in the Shiwaliks

b.x: **Structural zones (N → S):** Indus–Tsangpo Suture Zone (separates the Himalaya from **Tibet**) → Main Central Thrust → Main Boundary Thrust → **Himalayan Frontal Fault** (separates the Himalaya from the **plains**).
Significance

Blocks **Siberian cold waves**; shapes the **monsoon** pattern; its rivers and Shiwalik debris built the **Indo-Gangetic Plain's alluvium**. The **Plains** are the largest relief division of India (~43% of area).

**East v. west:** in the east the Himalaya rises **almost abruptly from the plains** over a narrow belt, so **Everest and Kanchenjunga** stand not far from the plains; in the west the ranges rise gradually across a wide belt.
